transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we prepare for the first case-management conference in three weeks, I need to make sure our draft litigation plan is solid before I approve it. The current draft preserves both asserted claims — claim 7 and claim 12 — seeks broad technical discovery, and permits source-code production under the opposing party's proposed protective order. Before I sign off, I'd like to hear from patent litigation counsel and our technology liaison: are there any facts or developments that should change this draft plan? I want to make sure we're not missing anything that would affect our claims strategy or discovery scope.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, there is a critical development. Yesterday, while reviewing a newly indexed prior-art collection, I found a published 2016 software implementation that anticipates every limitation of claim 7. Under our litigation policy, this requires claim 7 to be withdrawn from the asserted-claims strategy. I have not yet revised the draft plan because the prior-art collection was indexed after the plan circulated. My separate review found no equivalent anticipation of claim 12, so claim 12 should remain. This means the draft plan needs to be updated to withdraw claim 7 and limit discovery to material relevant to the surviving claim 12.

transcript.text: Elena, I have an important update regarding the source-code production provisions in the draft plan. This week I confirmed with the engineering security team that the opposing party's proposed protective order is inadequate for our source code. It allows two named employees of the opposing party to access produced code, but our board-approved security policy requires source-code access to be limited to outside counsel and independent experts who have signed enhanced source-code acknowledgments. I had not yet updated the litigation plan because the security team's confirmation arrived after our last legal-team meeting. This means the draft plan's acceptance of the opposing party's proposed protective order needs to be revised before approval to align with our security policy.
